title: Daily arXiv Biology and Biomedicine — 2026-11-06
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking, not a popularity ranking, and arXiv coverage of biomedical research is incomplete. Much experimental and clinical biology preprint research appears on bioRxiv or medRxiv.

sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: Friday’s 6 November 2026 arXiv biology/biomedicine batch yielded five notable papers from 15 eligible announcement records (14 new submissions and one revision). The strongest pattern is more rigorous evaluation of biological AI, alongside agent-assisted drug discovery with author-reported wet-lab follow-up. Spoken agenda: drug discovery, protein design, single-cell genomics, docking, and intracellular reaction networks.
sections.global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking, not a popularity ranking, and arXiv coverage of biomedical research is incomplete.

sections.title: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
sections.abstract: PharmAgents2 combines literature-derived decision knowledge and parallel agent exploration to produce drug-discovery candidates, with the authors reporting follow-up experiments for three discovery tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a 121-question benchmark and three research scenarios. They say 63 purchased compounds yielded an LpxH hit with enzyme-inhibition and biophysical binding evidence; 34 candidates were tested in two JAK1-related cytokine-signalling assays; and SPR supported binding of a proposed secondary target.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the LpxH binding site/mechanism and JAK1 selectivity/binding modes still need validation; these assays do not establish therapeutic efficacy or safety. The system-level study also does not isolate which agent component caused each outcome.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strong direct molecular-medicine relevance and author-reported biochemical, cellular, and binding-assay follow-up; these are relevance/contribution signals, not popularity measures.
sections.comment: 30 pages, 5 figures; includes references, appendices, and the NeurIPS checklist

sections.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding
sections.abstract: BILBY adds a larger PROSITE-derived motif-scaffolding benchmark and molecular-dynamics checks to test whether static protein-motif recovery corresponds to dynamical stability.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce BILBY-PRO (220 cases from 174 PROSITE motif-pattern entries) and BILBY-MD. Among 55 static successes assessed with MD, 31 met their MD-supported criterion and 8 passed all checks; they conclude static refolding alone does not establish scaffold dynamical fidelity.
sections.unique_caveat: MD support thresholds are heuristic, and 200 ns design trajectories may miss slower instabilities. BILBY-MD was applied to designs from the original MotifBench panel, not exhaustively to all BILBY-PRO cases; this is computational, not experimental functional validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct protein-design relevance; accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). The authors report a 220-case benchmark and a dynamics evaluation on 55 statically solved pairs.
sections.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). 23 pages, 10 figures, including supplementary material.

sections.title: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
sections.abstract: MUSS combines DNA-sequence representations, chromatin accessibility, and paired single-cell expression data to model regulatory patterns at cell and sequence scales.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report performance against sequence and single-cell baselines on expression prediction, enhancer–gene linking, motif-guided prioritization, and zero-shot cell clustering, including expression prediction for genes/peaks unseen during task training.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are computational; scores are not causal or clinical evidence. The authors note dependence on a substantial frozen sequence encoder and paired multi-omic data, quadratic attention cost, limited unseen-link evaluation, and single-run estimates for some expression outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strong genomics fit and q-bio.GN cross-listing; the arXiv record lists NeurIPS 2026, and a NeurIPS program entry and project code are publicly available. No verified citation-momentum signal was used.
sections.comment: 30 pages, 5 figures; includes references, appendices, and the NeurIPS checklist

sections.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking
sections.abstract: A fixed-budget DiffDock study compares broad continuation training with focused torsional supervision and finds no consistent advantage for the focused strategies on the reported docking endpoints.
sections.claimed_contribution: On a 99-complex evaluation with three training seeds, broad continuation had the highest mean trained-policy Top-1 success below 5 Å; focused or mixed supervision showed no consistent improvement over broad continuation under the tested budget.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a computational result for one architecture, one test set, and a five-epoch budget. The authors note that the confidence selector underperformed a uniform-random reference in the evaluated setting and that external/physical confirmation remains future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct molecular-docking relevance; accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD Workshop. The paper separates score fidelity, generated-pose recovery, best-of-10 recovery, and confidence-selected Top-1 performance.
sections.comment: 17 pages, 5 figures; accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD Workshop

sections.title: Accelerating reaction network identification via frequency-domain analysis
sections.abstract: The authors report that Fourier-domain measurements can make likelihoods approximately Gaussian in some intracellular reaction systems, enabling faster Bayesian network inference in an illustrative transcription example.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify a numerical condition under which a Fourier transform approximately Gaussianizes the measurement likelihood and use it to construct an accelerated Bayesian inference algorithm.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports an illustrative gene-transcription example, not broad experimental validation across biological systems; the approximation is stated to apply only to certain systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct molecular-network and intracellular-reaction relevance; primary category q-bio.MN. The abstract describes a gene-transcription example and a proposed acceleration over particle-filtering approaches.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Evaluation beyond one score or static structure recurs in BILBY and the DiffDock study. MUSS and the reaction-network paper contribute computational models spanning sequence, cell-level assays, and intracellular dynamics; neither establishes causality. PharmAgents2 reports human-executed assay follow-up for candidate generation, a single-paper observation rather than evidence of a field-wide trend.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: PharmAgents2's candidate activity and binding reports need orthogonal replication, selectivity panels, and further mechanism testing. BILBY motivates longer/replicate simulations and experimental stability/function checks. MUSS needs held-out cell types and perturbation tests; reaction-network inference needs comparisons across measured systems and noise regimes. Docking requires separate assessment of generation, confidence ranking, and external structural or binding validation.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The batch’s clearest signal is methodological: biological AI claims need evaluation beyond static prediction metrics. PharmAgents2 reports early experimental follow-up, not clinical validation. Popularity cannot be measured reliably from this small, very recent arXiv batch.
